intro.heading: VT Bench Probe
intro.text: An app-independent Servlet Filter for benchmarking virtual threads (Project Loom) vs. platform threads on this Sling instance.

what.heading: What
what.text:
VtBenchProbeFilter sleeps the current request thread for a configurable duration, simulating blocking I/O. Drive enough concurrent requests at it and you can watch the Sling/Jetty thread pool either park (virtual threads) or saturate (platform threads).

It is a single OSGi bundle — no ui.apps, no JCR content, no HTL. It has nothing to do with any specific app.

why.heading: Why a Filter, not a Sling Model + selector script
why.text:
The very first version of this lived inside sling-matrix as a Sling Model plus a vt-bench.html selector script under sling-matrix's own pages/basepage/. That meant it only worked on sling-matrix pages, and every other app that wanted to be benchmarked would need its own copy of the same script and model.

VtBenchProbeFilter is registered on the Sling filter whiteboard with sling.filter.scope=REQUEST, which runs it before resource resolution. That means it intercepts every request on the instance — any app, any path, even paths that don't resolve to a real resource — with zero per-app wiring.

enable.heading: How — enable it
enable.text:
Disabled by default (a sleep-on-demand endpoint has no business being live in production by accident):

http://localhost:8080/system/console/configMgr → "VT Bench Probe"
PID: org.motorbrot.vtbenchprobe.VtBenchProbeFilter

Config fieldDefaultMeaning
enabledfalsemaster on/off switch
queryParamName_vtbenchDelaypresence on ANY request triggers the probe; its value is the delay in ms
maxDelayMs5000safety cap — requested delay is clamped, so the probe can't hold a thread open indefinitely
renderRealPagefalsefalse: sleep, write a tiny plain-text body, stop. true: sleep, then continue to the real resource so it also renders.

use.heading: How — use it
use.text: Once enabled, append the query param to any URL on the instance. The response always carries X-VT-Bench-Thread (virtual/platform), X-VT-Bench-Delay-Ms, and X-VT-Bench-Elapsed-Ms headers, whether or not renderRealPage is on.

loadtest.heading: How — run the actual load test
loadtest.text: vt-bench.sh drives wrk (preferred) or hey against a list of URLs at increasing concurrency:

loadtest-preflight.text: It refuses to run silently against a disabled probe: a disabled filter still returns a normal HTTP 200 (the real page just renders), so the script checks for the X-VT-Bench-Thread response header first and tells you exactly how to enable it if that header is missing.

vt-knob.heading: How — turn on virtual threads (the CONGA knob)
vt-knob.text: Virtual threads are not a code change here — they're one config knob, rendered by CONGA (devops/conga) into JVM system properties:

vt-knob-yaml.code: # devops/conga/src/main/environments/local-plain.yaml config: httpVirtualThreads: true # or false httpThreadpoolMax: 200 # platform-thread ceiling (ignored when VT is on)

vt-knob-apply-example.code: cd devops/conga && mvn generate-resources cd launcher && ./launch.sh

vt-knob-result.text: This renders to devops/conga/target/configuration/local-plain/localhost/env/http-java-opts, picked up automatically by launcher/launch.sh:

vt-knob-prod.text: The same mechanism drives production — see the slingslop-runtime role config in prod-motorbrot.yaml.

jvm-params.heading: How — set custom JVM parameters
jvm-params.text:
Two ways to pass extra JVM flags to the local launcher, without editing launch.sh itself:

  • Ad-hoc, one-off flags — set EXTRA_JAVA_OPTS before launching (example below).
  • Persistent, environment-specific flags — add them to the CONGA environment's config: block (like httpVirtualThreads above) and render a new line in devops/conga/src/main/templates/slingslop-runtime/http-java-opts.hbs, so the flag is versioned and reproducible instead of typed by hand every time.

jvm-params-order.text: launch.sh assembles the final JAVA_OPTS as: base flags (G1GC, compact headers, string dedup) + JDWP (only if port 38080 is free) + EXTRA_JAVA_OPTS + the CONGA-rendered http-java-opts file, in that order — so both sources can add or override JVM system properties on the same run.
